Many people, perhaps yourself included, look at politics on a single axis: Left/Right. (In other words Socialist/Capitalist) To summarize it very briefly, this axis is about how much the State should tax.

Political debate has been entirely blinkered to examining another axis: Authority/Liberty. It is along this dimension that the Pirate Party clearly distinguishes itself. Here is a chart at the Political Compass website, depicting the various candidates for the US Primaries.

In most Western countries, the various political parties do not differ very much at all on Left-Right axis. What the Pirate Party want to do is offer an alternative to the Authoritarianism of the existing parties, the extent to which the government dictates what you can and can't do. The Pirate Party hopes to provide a less dictatorial way of helping a country run itself.

I imagine that since you don't like "socialist cucks", you are in favour of the Right. Perhaps you feel that such candidates offer you greater freedom. This is usually not the case. It tends to be that most right wingers are also more dictatorial. Have a look at this chart, showing famous politicians from history, or this one, showing how little current European governments differ.

Here is a suggestion, which I hope you might find fun and informative. You already feel comfortable denouncing people on the Left-Right axis (see "liberal cucks"). How about denouncing people along this other axis, the Authority/Liberty axis. You might have to use your imagination to create some diminishing terms for the sorts of people you don't like, but hey, that is fun, too!

In switching to watching and criticizing a different axis for a while, you might learn more about yourself, and become better acquainted with some of the issues which may previously have been off your radar.
